chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: 'Any man who buys from a man a sale, they both have the option (of rescinding) until they separate. So when they separate, the sale becomes binding.'

He said, and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'My father bought a land called Al-Urayz, so he purchased it from its owner for dinars. He said to him: I will give you silver (dirhams) with every dinar ten dirhams. So he sold it to him with it. So my father arose, and I followed him, so I said: O father! Why did you arise quickly? He said: I wanted that the sale would become binding.'
ai.seo_question: What is the rule regarding the right to cancel a sale before parties separate?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi codifies 'khiyar al-majlis' (option of the session), a fundamental principle in Shia jurisprudence allowing parties to nullify a contract before physical separation, thereby preventing hasty or regretful transactions. The narrative of Imam al-Sadiq’s father, Ja'far ibn Muhammad, illustrates the practical application of this rule, emphasizing that the binding nature of the sale is contingent upon the finality of the meeting. This ruling underscores the Islamic emphasis on mutual consent and clarity in commercial dealings, distinguishing it from later juristic debates regarding specific conditions of separation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Whichever man buys an item from a man, so they are both with the choice until they both separate. So when they separate, the item sold is binding’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘My<sup>asws</sup> father<sup>asws</sup> bought a land called Al-Urayz, so he<sup>asws</sup> purchased it from its owner for (some) Dinars. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> will give you one leaf (silver) of ten Dirhams with every Dinar’. So he sold it to him<sup>asws</sup> with it. So my<sup>asws</sup> father arose, and I<sup>asws</sup> followed him<sup>asws</sup>, so I<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘O father<sup>asws</sup>! Why did you<sup>asws</sup> arise quickly?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> wanted that the sale would become binding’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from af-Hafabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
If a man buys something from another man, he has the choice to dismiss the deal before they depart each other. When they depart the deal becomes binding.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, then said, ‘My father once purchased a piece of land called “al-‘Arid”. He purchased it for a few dinars and said to the seller. “I will give you a leaf (silver) for every dinar ten dirhams.” He purchased it and moved. I followed him and asked, “O father, why did you move so quickly?” He (the Imam) replied, “I wanted the transaction to become binding.’””
